criteria.evidence: Unchanged since round 1 (facts.ts summary schema, uniqueness, 1000-char cap); test 'a summary id equal to an entry or bullet id ... 400' passes at dcc25ee (local Postgres 16, full suite).

Summary rides the same verify and repair calls; tests 'first verify call ... PASSED with no extra call' and 'repair call ... REPAIRED' pass. Both prompts now state the word rule and one source per phrase (D36); they do not say that skill ids supply no words (low finding).

A copy of summaryPasses at dcc25ee returns false for every round-1 case ('The and of in.', 'Used Excel at Initech' citing skill:Excel+EXP-01, 'Built a revenue dashboard for 40 stores' from two bullets, 'Verified Rust experience.' citing stated skill:Rust), for Globex, Kubernetes, blank, dashes, 4 vs Q4, 2024 vs FY2024, 400, 40.5, no id and unknown id, and for splits by but/while/dash/em dash (unsplit, so stricter). A function-word-only clause next to a real one ('Of the. Built a revenue dashboard.') passes correctly. A skill-only summary ('Excel, SQL.' citing skill ids) is null because all skill ids, not only stated ones, supply no words. Positives kept: 'Cleaned sales data and built a revenue dashboard.', 'Cleaned data for 40 stores.', 'Data Analyst, Initech.', own summary id. Still true: a clause that is only a tool name, split off by with/and/', ', rides on a clause from another entry (medium finding).

dcc25ee changes only the deterministic check and prompt text, no call paths; call-count tests (2 normal, 4 max) pass.

The feature is live when the model follows the prompt rule; free-form wording is nulled.

findings.rule: c3 / Constitution I.1; D36 purpose (round-1 'Used Python at Saffron Retail' recombination)
findings.trigger: Splitting at with/and/', ' lets a bare tool clause from another entry attach to an employer or bullet: 'Data Analyst at Initech with Kotlin.' citing EXP-01 and PRJ-01-1 (Kotlin is a personal project) passes the copy; 'Compiled 460 pull requests in Jenkins and Kubernetes.' citing EXP-01-1 and SUM-01 (normal-001) passes; on the normal set 336/336 '<title> at <org> with <tool from another entry or the own summary>' pass, leaving only the verifier. Candidate fix tested on a copy: keep the clause rule, and also require all clauses of one sentence (split at . ! ? ; :) to rest on facts of one entry (the entry id and its bullet ids) or on the summary. It rejects 336/336 and every round-1 negative, keeps every positive in the test file, and lowers 'Title at Org with MH1 and MH2' from 73/73 to 12/73 and 'Skilled in <must-haves>' from 43/68 to 17/68. The lead may instead accept this as verifier-gated, since bullets have no tool check either.
findings.title: A tool-only clause split off by with/and/comma recombines a tool from another entry with an employer
findings.proof: Summary 'Data Analyst at Initech with Kotlin.' citing EXP-01 and PRJ-01-1, verifier supported for all; expect result.summary null.

findings.rule: D36: the generate and repair prompts state the rule; D36 removes words only from stated-skill labels
findings.trigger: summaryClause invites 'skill ids' as sources and says to use only words from the cited sources, and the repair item lists skill texts as sources, but summaryPasses drops every skill: id (not only stated ones). 'Skilled in Excel and SQL.' or 'Excel, SQL.' citing skill:Excel and skill:SQL fails both the first check and the repair, so the summary is null. Either say in both prompts that skill names count only when a cited entry, bullet or the summary holds them, or let a non-stated skill id supply its bare name as D36 states.
findings.title: Prompts offer skill ids as word sources that the check never accepts
